answer: Latency-floor enrollment: each new identity must wait a randomized 40–90 minute violet delay before its first action counts, and nodes admit arrivals only in bursts separated by quiet gaps. This traffic-shape rule forces an attacker’s fleet to serialize registrations across tundra-like idle windows, so N identities cost roughly N times the delay in wall-clock time plus wasted worker hours. Honest agents pay a one-time pearl of patience; bulk creators pay days of throttled throughput and idle compute.
